LESSON: DEMOCRACY IN SCHOOL

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Citizenship and Governance in Kenya
Topic 5.4: Democracy in school

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Democracy in school. Read, look at the pictures, practise, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: LEARN

BENEFITS OF DEMOCRACY IN SCHOOL [ ] Hallo learner, welcome to a social studies lesson for grade 4. Today we shall learn about benefits of democracy in school. [ ]

Hallo learner, welcome to our social studies lesson for grade 4. Today we shall learn about benefits of democracy in school. So get your book and pencil and let us learn social studies. I am your radio teacher Eugene Kimani. [ ] I hope you have your book and pen ready and set to learn. We are going to start the lesson by remembering what we learnt about factors that promote peace in school. What did we say about factors that promote peace in school? [ ] Very good, we said the factors that promote peace in school include: love, respect, kindness, caring, hard work, peace, tolerance and obedience Today we are going to learn about benefits of democracy in school. Now what is democracy? Answer when you hear the. [ ] Very good, democracy is a situation where we are allowed to take part in making decisions on issues that affect us. In which ways do you think we can practise democracy in school? Answer when you hear the. [ ] Very good, we can practise democracy in the following ways: Choosing our leaders. Making class rules. Taking part in class discussions. Sharing duties. Taking part in debates. I will repeat, we can practise democracy in the following ways: Choosing our leaders. Making class rules. Taking part in class discussions. Sharing duties. Taking part in debates. Now, why do you think it is important to practice democracy in school? Answer when you hear the. [ ] Very good, it is important to practice democracy in school because: Learners are able to say their ideas without fear. The school performs well when teachers are allowed to teach the subjects they are good at. Learners feel that they are part of the school when they take part in making decisions on issues affecting them. Learners are able to choose the leaders they feel have good leadership qualities. Learners who are chosen as leaders are prepared for future leadership roles.

Democracy encourages peace and harmony in school. When there is democracy in school, people treat each other fairly. Learner I will give you a small exercise. Say democracy or no democracy in these sentences I will read for you. Say democracy or no democracy, when I read each sentence. Do that when you hear the. Your parent allows you to say what you feel. Democracy or no democracy. [Bell] Your teacher allows you to answer questions. Democracy or no democracy. [Bell] Learners are not allowed to raise their hands in class. Democracy or no democracy. [Bell] Learner, I hope you were able to answer. Let us look at the sentences. Your parent allows you to say what you feel. Here, there is Democracy. Your teacher allows you to answer questions. Your teacher is practicing Democracy. Learners are not allowed to raise their hands in class. There is no Democracy here because learners are not allowed to be free and say what they think. This is your homework. How do you support student leaders in school? How do you support student leaders in school? Write down the answers and read them out to your parent or guardian. That is the end of our lesson for today. [ ] You have been listening to a social studies programme for grade 4 learners. Your radio teacher was Eugene Kimani. This programme was recorded by John Mbiti. Until next time, Goodbye. [ ]

SECTION 3: TRY THIS

1. Look again at the examples or pictures above.
2. Tell a parent or friend what Democracy in school means, using your own words.
3. Copy one example into your exercise book and change it to fit your school or home.
4. Underline three new words and find out what they mean.

SECTION 4: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Democracy in school.
2. Complete any “Work to do” items shown in the pupil book pages above.
3. Create three of your own practice questions on this topic.
4. Answer the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after finishing.

SECTION 5: REMEMBER

1. Topic: Democracy in school
2. Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
3. Learning materials: SST_PROGRAMME_13 BENEFITS OF DEMOCRACY IN SCHOOL; PROGRAMME_10 QUALITIES OF GOOD CITIZENSHIP IN SCHOOL; PROGRAMME_2 THE SCHOOL
4. Revise with the quiz now.

— CBC Learn · Learner lesson
